commit_message:
[Merged] Bug 1948203 - Skip alt-svc validation if we already connected to the server, r=necko-reviewers,jesup

This patch optimizes how Firefox handles speculative connections for alt-svc headers. When a server sends an alt-svc header, Firefox normally creates a speculative connection to validate it. With this patch, if the connection’s hash key matches the one generated from the alt-svc header, the validation step is skipped since an equivalent connection is already in place, avoiding unnecessary work.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D238218

fix_commit_message:
Bug 1951554 - Avoid racing on nsHttpTransaction::mConnInfo, r=necko-reviewers,valentin

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D243146
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix d3c35516e9e8 on top of intro 52d7d34ee0f9 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (DataRace): The `GetConnInfo()` method reads `mConnInfo` on the main thread without holding a lock, while `DisableHttp3()` modifies `mConnInfo` via `mConnInfo.swap(connInfo)` on the socket thread. This creates a data race condition. The ThreadSanitizer detected a read of size 8 on the main thread in `GetConnInfo` concurrent with a write of size 8 on thread T7 in `DisableHttp3`. This can lead to use-after-free or reading corrupted pointer values, potentially causing crashes or undefined behavior. Root cause: Bug 1948203 introduced a new call to mTransaction->GetConnInfo() in nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse1() on the main thread to pass connection information to ProcessAltService(). However, mConnInfo in nsHttpTransaction was already being modified by DisableHttp3() on the socket thread without synchronization. The pre-existing code paths didn't have this cross-thread access pattern, making the race condition a regression introduced by this optimization patch.
